reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator 'offensive line drag' is a regression-derived measure of how much a team's scoring deviates when key tackles are absent. It is computed as the difference between actual points scored and what that opponent typically allows. This is modeled over 1069 team-weeks, ensuring statistical robustness. The 'tackle absence coefficient' quantifies the impact of each tackle status (out, dnp, limited) on this deviation. These coefficients are subject to two forms of regularization: first, those within one standard error or positive are set to zero, reflecting Bayesian prior belief in insignificance; second, coefficients exceeding 7 points in absolute value are shrunk toward zero, mitigating noise-induced overestimation. The model assumes self-comparison (each team vs. itself), which removes confounding variables. The failure mode arises from overfitting if too many variables are included without sufficient data, or misclassification of absence tags such as pooling doubtful with out. The system is designed to be retroactively consistent, reading previous week’s results to inform current modeling.
